title: Swap Odd and Even Bits
description: Given a 32-bit signed integer `n`, swap every pair of adjacent bits in its 32-bit two's complement binary representation: swap bit `0` with bit `1`, bit `2` with bit `3`, and so on up to bit `30` with bit `31`. Return the resulting 32-bit signed integer.
hints: Mask all odd-indexed bits with `0xAAAAAAAA` and shift them right logically (unsigned) by `1`; mask all even-indexed bits with `0x55555555` and shift them left by `1`.
Combine both shifted halves with bitwise OR, taking care to interpret the 32-bit result as a signed two's complement integer.

examples.explanation: 23 is 010111 in binary; swapping adjacent pairs (01)(01)(11) produces (10)(10)(11) = 43.
2 is 10 in binary; swapping bits 0 and 1 gives 01 = 1.
-1 has all 32 bits set to 1, so swapping adjacent bits leaves it unchanged as -1.
